1. (Currently amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value, __wherein the pump is driven by an engine and the method further comprises reducing parasitic load on the engine by reducing a pressure differential across the pump__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, __and wherein the directional control valve is actuated based on a pressure sensor signal indicating that the predetermined value has been reached__.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __wherein the directional control valve is a three-way valve__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __wherein the negative pressure chamber is in fluid communication with the booster device and the positive pressure chamber is upstream of the pump__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere, __wherein the pump outlet is vented to atmosphere to reduce the pressure differential across the pump__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 5, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter, __wherein the filter is positioned in the vent path to prevent contaminants from entering the pump__.

7. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

8. (Currently amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced; __and a pressure sensor configured to detect when the level of vacuum has reached the predetermined value and signal the directional control valve to actuate__.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __wherein the directional control valve is a three-way valve with two positions__.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __wherein the negative pressure chamber is in fluid communication with the booster device__.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, __wherein the pump outlet is vented to atmosphere__.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, __wherein the filter is positioned in the vent path to prevent contaminants from entering the pump__.

13. (Original) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

14. (Currently amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device, __the pump being mechanically driven by the internal combustion engine__; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced, __wherein the directional control valve is actuated by a pressure-responsive mechanism that detects when the predetermined vacuum level is reached__.

15. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __wherein the directional control valve is a three-way valve__.

16. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __wherein the negative pressure chamber is in fluid communication with the booster device__.

17. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, __wherein the pump outlet is vented to atmosphere__.

18. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 17, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, __wherein the filter is positioned in the vent path to prevent contaminants from entering the pump__.

19. (Original) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system.

20. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the engine is a compression-ignition type, __and wherein the pump is sized and configured to establish the predetermined vacuum level within a specified time period for the compression-ignition engine__.
